key_insight: Benchmarking a universal machine-learning interatomic potential enables large-scale finite-temperature simulations that capture the star-of-David to hexagonal charge-density-wave transition in monolayer 1T-TaS2.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable workflow for predicting structural phase behavior in CDW materials beyond what conventional DFT molecular dynamics can practically access.
method: Benchmark UMA-s-1p1 MLIPs against DFT displacement energies
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across temperature cycles
Use temperature-dependent effective potential phonon calculations to analyze vibrational/structural signatures
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the selected UMA-s-1p1 potential matched DFT well enough for finite-temperature MD and reproduced the experimentally observed phase-transition sequence, including thermal hysteresis and multi-domain freezing on cooling.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on careful MLIP benchmarking and transferability; insufficient validation could miss subtle CDW domain or chirality effects.
paper_title: Charge-Density-Wave Phase Transitions in Monolayer 1T-TaS2 from Universal Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
